body.statement: The finite-dimensional inversion has the following exact scope.  If the first-stage regions satisfy \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\mathsf P\in\mathfrak M_H}\mathsf P\{((r_{bt}),(q_w))\in\mathcal I_{n,\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\), then \(\text{thm:confidence-polytope}\) gives the same uniform asymptotic outer coverage for \(\mathcal V(p_{BT},q)\) and \(\mathcal M^\star\), including simultaneous Hall equalities and arbitrary policy ties.  However, coarsening at random, pointwise censoring positivity, and the phrase ``multiply robust nuisance estimation'' alone cannot yield nonvacuous uniformly shrinking inference.  For every \(H\ge2\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\), any uniformly honest sequence of observed-data confidence regions for the whole value set has a sequence of laws in \(\mathfrak M_H\) along which its sup-norm diameter is at least \(H\) with limiting probability at least \(1-2\alpha\).  Already for \(H=3\) and \(\mathcal M=\{1,2,3\}\), any uniformly honest outer confidence set for \(\mathcal M^\star\) has a sequence along which it contains both thresholds \(1\) and \(3\) with limiting probability at least \(1-2\alpha\).  Thus a nonvacuous cross-fitted implementation of \(\mathfrak I\) requires quantitative conditions that exclude the displayed vanishing-information sequences and control nuisance remainders; standard sufficient conditions would include uniform effective assignment, survival, and censoring overlap together with uniform cross-fitted rate conditions, none of which is supplied by the frozen assumptions.
body.proof_tex:
The positive conditional assertion is set-theoretic.  For every \(\mathsf P\in\mathfrak M_H\), \(\text{thm:confidence-polytope}\) gives
\[
 \{((r_{bt}),(q_w))\in\mathcal I_{n,\alpha}\}
 \subseteq
 \{\mathcal V(p_{BT},q)\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal V}_{n,\alpha},\ 
   \mathcal M^\star\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal M}_{n,\alpha}\}.       \tag{1}
\]
Taking probabilities, then the infimum over \(\mathfrak M_H\), and finally the lower limit proves the asserted uniform outer coverage.  Because (1) uses only weak inequalities and inclusion, simultaneous Hall equalities and arbitrary policy ties require no separate regularity condition.

We next give an explicit two-law obstruction to uniformly shrinking whole-set inference.  Fix \(H\ge2\), put \(\epsilon_n=n^{-2}>0\), and construct two laws with \(\mathsf P(R=1)=1/2\), no death, \(S_k^0=S_k^1=1\), \(B=0\), and switched residual \(W=0\).  Under law zero set \(T=0\) almost surely; under law one set \(T=H\) almost surely.  Give the standard sustained branch raw residual zero.  Observe every subject through \(k\); independently of the response tree and assignment, set \(C=K\) with probability \(\epsilon_n\) and \(C=k\) otherwise.  The only nonunit censoring continuation probability is \(\epsilon_n>0\).  Independence gives factual-arm sequential coarsening at random, assignment is independent of the response tree, assignment and landmark survival are positive, and \(B+W=0\le H\).  The cap-fibre lift in \(\text{thm:causal-response-tree-lift}\) completes legal raw-count branches while preserving the observed pushforward.  Thus both laws lie in \(\mathfrak M_H\); no uniform overlap constant has been added.

For every \(m\in\mathcal M\subseteq\{1,\ldots,H\}\), \(B<m\) and \(\pi=1\).  Hence the two sharp value sets are
\[
 V_0=\{(0)_{m\in\mathcal M}\},\qquad
 V_1=\{(H)_{m\in\mathcal M}\}.                           \tag{2}
\]
Couple one observation under the two laws using the same assignment, censoring draw, and all histories through \(k\).  Coupled observations can differ only when \(R=1\) and \(C=K\), an event of probability \(\epsilon_n/2\).  Coordinatewise coupling of \(n\) observations and the union bound give
\[
 \lVert P_{0,n}^{\otimes n}-P_{1,n}^{\otimes n}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le n\epsilon_n/2=(2n)^{-1}\longrightarrow0.             \tag{3}
\]

Let \(\mathcal C_n\) be any observed-data random region with uniform asymptotic whole-value-set coverage at level \(1-\alpha\).  Applied to the two triangular sequences, uniform honesty gives
\[
 P_{0,n}^{\otimes n}(V_0\subseteq\mathcal C_n)\ge1-\alpha-o(1),\qquad
 P_{1,n}^{\otimes n}(V_1\subseteq\mathcal C_n)\ge1-\alpha-o(1).        \tag{4}
\]
Total variation in (3) transfers the second event to law zero with an \(o(1)\) loss.  A union bound under law zero then gives
\[
 P_{0,n}^{\otimes n}\{V_0\cup V_1\subseteq\mathcal C_n\}
 \ge1-2\alpha-o(1).                                      \tag{5}
\]
On this event, \(\operatorname{diam}_{\infty}(\mathcal C_n)\ge H\) by (2), proving the whole-value-set obstruction.

For the optimizer obstruction, set \(H=3\), \(\mathcal M=\{1,2,3\}\), and use the common \((p,q)\) margins of \(\mathsf E_3\).  Their nontrivial Hall slacks are \((1/5,3/10,1/5)\), so a legal capacity coupling exists with strict slack.  In law zero put \(T=0\) in every row.  Capacity forces row \(b=3\) into column zero, so \(J_3=0\) under every compatible coupling, and nonnegativity gives \(J_1,J_2\ge0\).  Therefore \(R_3=0\).  The feasible plan
\[
 x_{00}=\frac15,\quad x_{03}=\frac15,\quad
 x_{11}=\frac1{10},\quad x_{12}=\frac15,\quad
 x_{21}=\frac15,\quad x_{30}=\frac1{10}                  \tag{6}
\]
has the required row and column margins, satisfies \(b+w\le3\), and yields
\((J_1,J_2,J_3)=(7/10,1/5,0)\).  Hence
\(R_1\ge D_{13}\ge7/10\) and \(R_2\ge D_{23}\ge1/5\), proving
\[
 \mathcal M^\star_0=\{3\}.                               \tag{7}
\]

In law one, conditional on \(B=1\), put probabilities \(5/6\) and \(1/6\) on \(T=1\) and \(T=2\); conditional on \(B=2\), put probabilities \(1/8\) and \(7/8\) on \(T=0\) and \(T=1\); and set \(T=0\) in rows zero and three.  Multiplication by the row masses gives
\[
 (\mu_0,\mu_1,\mu_2,\mu_3)=(0,7/20,7/40,0),              \tag{8}
\]
so \(\text{prop:rational-recommendation-reversal}\) gives
\(\mathcal M^\star_1=\{1\}\).  The common \(p\) margin permits identical pre-landmark intensive histories, and the standard sustained histories and switched margins can also be identical.  The response-tree lift supplies all unused branches.  Under the same censoring scheme the coupled observations can again differ only when \(R=1,C=K\), so (3) remains valid.

Let \(\mathcal K_n\subseteq\mathcal M\) be any uniformly honest outer confidence set for \(\mathcal M^\star\).  Coverage of the two unique optimizers, total-variation transfer, and the union bound give
\[
 P_{0,n}^{\otimes n}\{\{1,3\}\subseteq\mathcal K_n\}
 \ge1-2\alpha-o(1).                                      \tag{9}
\]
The two laws have strict Hall slack and unique optimizers; their only vanishing information is the probability \(\epsilon_n\) of observing post-landmark intensive outcomes.  Since \(\epsilon_n\) is positive for each \(n\), the sequence lies in the pointwise-overlap class \(\mathfrak M_H\), but it is excluded from every submodel imposing a fixed positive lower bound on factual censoring continuation.  This proves the claimed limitation.
body.justification: The theorem isolates the information-theoretic obstruction in the unchanged pointwise-overlap model by constructing total-variation-indistinguishable laws whose value sets or unique robust thresholds remain separated.
body.gap: Sequential CAR, pointwise positivity, and recurrent-event multiply robust estimation do not by themselves answer whether honest confidence regions can shrink uniformly when post-landmark observation probabilities approach zero.
body.consumer: Investigators must either verify a quantitative overlap and nuisance-rate submodel before using the positive cross-fitted result or report the broader-class nonshrinkage limitation; Hall slack and unique policies do not cure vanishing information.
